doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First international tour and traveling abroad
summary: He cannot recall his first overseas trip but remembers Europe, Japan, Brazil and the Caribbean.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When did you have your first international tour, going to either to Europe or…?
Okay. Do you remember going as a leader or as a sideman>
Oh, I don’t know, let me think. That’s an interesting question, I don’t remember, at the moment I can’t remember if I was a leader or a sideman. I know I spent many trips over there.
I was just wondering what is that first, you know, coming out of Detroit, of course, you’ve toured nationally already. But coming over seas and seeing other folks that are so embracing of your music…
Right. Brown:…and unconditional acceptance, not like in America.

You have to forgive me, but at this moment I’m drawing a blank, I don’t know maybe, for whatever reason. But I do know that I felt very encouraged whenever I went to Europe and Japan and I made two trips to Brazil and it was nice. A couple of trips to the Caribbean. But it was always good because you have some real jazz fans all over the world, parts of the world, they were really nice. I’m sorry I can’t remember the…
No problem, that’s alright, that’s alright.
I’m sure it’s there somewhere, I just have to unlock it and I can’t unlock it at the moment.
